task: CV-31 — Paid Entitlement → Real Runtime E2E
phase: Architecture review only (read-only, design approval gate)
rule: DO NOT modify code, DO NOT create migrations, DO NOT add tests, DO NOT refactor. No install, no signup, no payment, no API calls until plan is approved.

actual_cli_lifecycle_in_v1_3_0.summary: npm client is a CUSTOMER-FACING CLI. It does NOT contain signup, login, checkout-payment-capture, or in-CLI webhooks. Payment and account creation happen on the web (minitok.dev). The CLI starts AFTER the customer has a JWT from checkout.

commands.doctor: Environment check (Node, git, providers, ~/.minitok). Does NOT contact server.
commands.migrate: Local: writes minitok.yml + .minitok/ + registers workspace. No network. No entitlement check.
commands.status: Local: reads ~/.minitok/entitlement/* and prints state. No network unless online path used. Reports Entitlement: ALLOWED|MISSING|EXPIRED|...
commands.checkout: POST /v1/checkout/dodo with a pre-existing customer JWT → returns a checkout_url to open in a browser. CLI never captures payment.
commands.activation-key: POST /v1/activation-key with the JWT (and optional dodo_payment_id) → returns activation_key exactly once. Requires JWT from prior signup/purchase.
commands.activate: POST /v1/activate { key, installation_id, hostname } → stores signed entitlement + installation_token locally. This is what makes the local gate pass.
commands.auth login <provider>: Stores LLM provider API key or runs OAuth. NOT customer auth — it is provider credential storage.
commands.portal: POST /v1/portal/dodo with JWT → returns billing portal URL.
commands.run <task>: Loads config, REQUIRES entitlement gate to pass (calls checkEntitlementOnline, refuses if not allowed), then runs plan→implement→verify with an LLM provider. Needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY / GOOGLE_API_KEY / OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
commands.runtime start|stop|status: Local HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:4578. Endpoints: /health, GET /api/v1/status, POST /api/v1/{knowledge/query,knowledge/record,knowledge/analyze,context/compact,evidence/collect,observations/ingest,observations/query,audit/recent}.

what_is_NOT_in_the_cli: login (no customer-login CLI command — the JWT is issued at checkout time)
webhook receiver (lives on the server, not the client)

payment_to_runtime_wiring.1_checkout: minitok checkout --token <JWT> [--plan pro] → POST https://api.minitok.dev/v1/checkout/dodo → { checkout_url }. User opens URL in browser. Dodo webhook → server records subscription.
payment_to_runtime_wiring.2_activation_key: minitok activation-key --token <JWT> [--payment <dodo_payment_id>] → POST /v1/activation-key → { activation_key } (one-time). Server validates webhook-driven subscription state.
payment_to_runtime_wiring.3_activate: minitok activate <activation_key> → POST /v1/activate { key, installation_id, hostname } → { entitlement (signed), installation_token }. Client writes ~/.minitok/entitlement/entitlement.json + installation-token.json. Server stores installation_id ↔ subscription.
payment_to_runtime_wiring.4_entitlement_gate: Local: verify.js validates Ed25519 signature over canonical payload, checks installation_id binding (v1.3.0), expiry, clock rollback. Online: checkEntitlementOnline also POSTs /v1/validate to server with installation_token (server may downgrade state to SERVER_REJECTED).
payment_to_runtime_wiring.5_runtime_start: minitok runtime start → starts 127.0.0.1:4578 with NO entitlement gate. RuntimeService.status() only reads gate state. Every other endpoint accepts requests regardless of state.
payment_to_runtime_wiring.6_run: minitok run <task> → runPipeline throws if !allowed. This is the ONLY command that hard-blocks on entitlement state.
payment_to_runtime_wiring.7_actual_supported_provider_task: Step 13 of CV-31 requires a real LLM provider call. The package's supported providers are anthropic, openai, google, openrouter, plus tier-3 custom. ALL require an API key.

forbidden_terms_anti_legacy_check.rule: DO NOT use any legacy/stripped identifier. The npm package has been proprietary since 1.2.0; all pre-1.2.0 MIT versions are deprecated. Stripe is retained only via opt-in (portal --stripe, /v1/portal).
terms_to_avoid_in_production_path: pip install minitok (npm path is the commercial client)
KEYS = key-2024-01-prod via the OLD public-key file path if it conflicts with v1.1.4 fixed key
offline grace of 30 days (v1.3.0 CHANGELOG says enforced but gate.js source shows OFFLINE_GRACE_DAYS=0 — see GAP #1)
forbidden_terms_anti_legacy_check.grep_method: function-declaration-start patterns (^func_name), not substrings. Avoid false positives from comments.

critical_findings.title: Runtime server has NO per-request entitlement gate
critical_findings.evidence: src/runtime/routes.js — every endpoint (knowledge/query, knowledge/record, knowledge/analyze, context/compact, evidence/collect, observations/ingest, observations/query, audit/recent) accepts requests without checking entitlement. EntitlementService.status() is only called for /api/v1/status (informational).
critical_findings.implication: CV-31 step 'runtime without entitlement' will show that the runtime process STARTS, and all MCP endpoints RESPOND, when no entitlement is present. This is by design per README ('localhost-only, no authentication required') but the user's verification expects a denial.
critical_findings.what_user_actually_gets: Runtime start = process up, port 4578 listening. /health = 200. /api/v1/status = 200 with entitlement.state='MISSING'. Other endpoints = 200 with empty/default data. The hard block is only at minitok run, not at the runtime.

critical_findings.title: CHANGELOG claim vs source code for offline grace
critical_findings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md 1.1.0: 'Offline grace mode (30 days) for expired entitlements'. src/entitlement/gate.js line 18-19: 'const OFFLINE_GRACE_DAYS = 0; const OFFLINE_GRACE_MS = 0;'
critical_findings.implication: The OFFLINE_GRACE state exists but is unreachable in the shipped code path because the constant is zero. Re-verify in run.

critical_findings.title: No CLI signup/login/payment-capture
critical_findings.evidence: bin/minitok.js — no 'signup' or 'login' command. checkout.js only opens a Dodo checkout URL in the browser and never captures payment data.
critical_findings.implication: CV-31 steps 4-7 (signup, login, checkout, payment) cannot be performed end-to-end via the CLI alone. They require the minitok.dev web flow + Dodo sandbox/live. We can: (a) sign up on the web with a disposable email, (b) obtain the JWT, (c) drive the remaining CLI steps. The CV-31 procedure is misaligned with the product — the CLI begins AT checkout, not BEFORE.

critical_findings.title: Step 13 (real supported provider task) needs a real LLM API key
critical_findings.evidence: src/pipeline/loop.js line 144-146: 'Provider is not available. Set the appropriate API key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, or GOOGLE_API_KEY).'
critical_findings.implication: Cannot run a real task without a real API key. Per CV-31: '실제 supported provider가 없다면 mock으로 PASS 처리하지 마십시오. provider credential이 필요하면 BLOCKED로 기록하십시오.' → this is a hard BLOCKED gate. Operator must supply a key.

critical_findings.title: Step 8-9 require a real paid activation key
critical_findings.evidence: minitok activation-key requires a JWT that the server only issues after a successful Dodo checkout webhook. minitok activate calls POST /v1/activate which the server only honors for keys tied to a real subscription.
critical_findings.implication: Cannot complete steps 6-9 without (a) disposable account on minitok.dev, (b) Dodo sandbox or test-mode payment, (c) real activation_key returned from /v1/activation-key. Per taste rule: BLOCKED — operator credential required.

critical_findings.title: Runtime start is a foreground blocking process
critical_findings.evidence: src/cli/commands/runtime.js: cmdRuntimeStart returns 'new Promise(() => {})' — it never resolves. minitok runtime start blocks the terminal until killed.
critical_findings.implication: For CV-31 step 11 we must background it (Windows: START /B or PowerShell Start-Process). For step 14 (stop) we need to send SIGTERM; on Windows the npm package uses process.kill which on Windows only supports SIGTERM as termination signal (no actual SIGTERM semantics).

PASS: v1.3.0 is published and matches the README
CLI surface (doctor, migrate, status, checkout, activation-key, activate, runtime, run) is consistent across bin/minitok.js, src/cli/commands/*, and README
Entitlement gate is enforced in runPipeline (the only command that actually performs work)
Ed25519 signature verification is present (src/entitlement/verify.js) with installation_id binding in v1.3.0
Runtime binds 127.0.0.1 only (HOST constant in runtime/server.js)
GAP: GAP-1: runtime has no per-request gate (design vs verification expectation mismatch)
GAP-3: CLI has no signup/login; web step is required
GAP-4: real LLM key required for step 13 → BLOCKED
GAP-5: real paid activation_key required for steps 6-9 → BLOCKED
GAP-6: Windows process kill semantics differ from POSIX (use taskkill)
RISK: Disposable account + Dodo sandbox: webhook delivery latency could leave the JWT/subscription out of sync with the /v1/activation-key response. Idempotency must be verified by replay.
CV-31 step 8 'activation key' is a string the server returns once. If the run fails mid-way, re-running activation-key will return 'already retrieved' (or null). Capture on first success.
v1.3.0 binds entitlements to installation_id. A 'clean Windows user/home' run means a fresh installation_id — re-activation is required, not portable from a prior machine.

Q2: Do you have a real LLM API key (Anthropic / OpenAI / Google / OpenRouter) for step 13? [Y/N — if N, step 13 is BLOCKED]

Q3: Do you want the runtime to be a hard requirement for step 13, or is the verification that 'runtime started with valid entitlement' enough on its own? — affects whether to skip the expensive provider call
Q4: Confirm target directory: C:\Users\J1\cv31-paid-runtime (clean dir, fresh `git init`)?

recommendation:
Approve the architecture review and execution plan as-is, with the following conditions:
  1. Operator answers Q1-Q4 (esp. confirmation of Dodo test-mode payment and LLM API key availability)
  2. Idempotency verification (replay activation-key) is a mandatory step, not optional
  3. Step 13 (real provider task) MUST be marked BLOCKED if no real key is supplied — never mock-PASS
  4. Report is written to docs/CV-31_PAID_RUNTIME_E2E_REPORT.md only AFTER the operator signs off, in chunked stages per taste rule (index first, then one Part per response)

Compare pros/cons of two execution postures:
  A) Execute the entire 15-step plan end-to-end on operator go-ahead
  B) Execute only up to phase_h (entitlement granted) first, then return for go-ahead on runtime + provider call
Recommend B (gate after phase_h) so the operator can inspect a real ALLOWED entitlement + activation_key artifact before spending on an LLM call, and so a webhook/activation failure doesn't burn the LLM budget.
